title: The affine line
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside it. Let $V$ be a separated scheme of finite type over $k$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], and let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$. For $E$ use its continuous-function condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]; for $\Qlb$ use the condensed ring of continuous functions with values in some finite subextension [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. The coefficient ring on a scheme $X$ is its pullback $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\underline\Lambda$ from the point [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Let $p:\mathbf A^1_V\to V$ be the affine-line projection [def-nagata-relative-affine-space], $j:\mathbf A^1_V\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1_V$ the standard open immersion, and $q:\mathbf P^1_V\to V$ the projective-line projection [def-nagata-relative-projective-space], so $p=q\circ j$.

Use the ambient module-object derived categories and derived pullbacks of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], bounded constructible complexes $\Dbc$ of [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and localizing closure as in [sk-def-localizing-closure]. The functor $Rp_!$ is the compactification functor of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek], and $p^!$ is its right adjoint on the localizing closures from [sk-prop-sf-existence]. Write $K(1)=K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Lambda_X}\Lambda_X(1)$ for the Tate twist of [sk-def-sp-tate-twist], and $[2]$ for cohomological shift. Then:

1. $j_!$ and $j^*$ preserve the respective categories $\Loc(\Dbc(-,\Lambda))$, and their restrictions satisfy $j_!\dashv j^*$;
2. $Rp_!\simeq Rq_*\circ j_!$ on these categories;
3. $Rp_!$ is left adjoint to $p^*(1)[2]$, and there is a natural isomorphism
$$
p^!\simeq p^*(1)[2]:\Loc(\Dbc(V,\Lambda))\longrightarrow\Loc(\Dbc(\mathbf A^1_V,\Lambda)),
$$
uniquely determined by compatibility with the two adjunction counits.

proof.text: The standard-chart theorem [lemma-nagata-relative-affine-space-open-immersion] identifies $j$ with $D_+(T_0)\subset\mathbf P^1_V$, over $V$, so $qj=p$. Properness [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], using the two homogeneous coordinates $\{0,1\}$ in [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], gives that $q$ is proper. The chart description also checks quasi-compactness of $j$: above an affine $W=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset V$, its intersection with the $T_0$ chart is the whole $\operatorname{Spec}R[t]$, and with the $T_1$ chart is the principal open $D(s)\subset\operatorname{Spec}R[s]$, where $s=T_0/T_1$; both are affine, hence quasi-compact. On each chart the restricted inclusion is respectively the identity or the principal-open immersion $\operatorname{Spec}R[s,s^{-1}]\to\operatorname{Spec}R[s]$, hence an affine morphism and quasi-compact (inverse images of affine opens for a localization are affine). These charts cover $\mathbf P^1_V$, so [lem-pc-quasi-compact-local-on-target] proves that $j$ is quasi-compact. Thus $(j,q)$ is a compactification by [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data]. All three schemes are qcqs: $V$ is quasi-compact by finite type and quasi-separated by separatedness; a finite affine cover of $V$ gives a finite affine cover of $\mathbf A^1_V$ and, with two charts over each member, of $\mathbf P^1_V$. The affine-line diagonal is cut out over each $W$ by $t_1-t_2$, so the affine line is separated over $V$; the projective line is separated over $V$ because $q$ is proper. For either $X=\mathbf A^1_V$ or $X=\mathbf P^1_V$, its diagonal over $k$ factors through $X\times_VX$: the second map is the inverse image of the closed diagonal of $V/k$, and the first is its closed diagonal over $V$. Locally the two closed subscheme equations combine by adding their ideals, so the composite is closed. Thus both schemes are separated over $k$. Their polynomial charts give finite type over $k$: adjoining the single chart variable to any finite set of generators of an affine base algebra still gives a finite generating set. Hence they remain in the standing setting.

source.place: Proof (2): verify the standard compactification and the qcqs hypotheses used in (1)–(3).

proof.text: For $X=V,\mathbf A^1_V,\mathbf P^1_V$, apply [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc] to the qcqs scheme $X$ and $\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$, obtaining $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)=\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ and equality of their localizing closures. Clause 1 of [det-sf-mate-open-restriction], with the quasi-compact open $j$ and qcqs target verified in step 1, gives functors $j_!$ and $j^*$ between the corresponding $\Loc(\Dctf)$ categories and $j_!\dashv j^*$. Replacing these full subcategories by the equal $\Loc(\Dbc)$ subcategories proves (1). Only clause 1 of that node is used.

source.place: Proof (1): preservation and restricted open adjunction, using the existing stronger open-immersion statement.

proof.text: For the compactification $c=(j,q)$ of step 1, the definition [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek] gives $Rp_!^c=Rq_*D(j_!)$. The functor of [sk-prop-sf-existence] is defined using a chosen compactification $c_p$. Apply [det-sf-comp-coherence-cocycle] to $p$, $c_p$ and $c$; $p$ is separated of finite type and its target $V$ is qcqs, as checked in step 1. It gives a natural isomorphism $Rp_!^{c_p}\simeq Rp_!^c$ on $\Loc(\Dctf)$. The equalities of categories in step 2 give $Rp_!\simeq Rq_*j_!$ on the claimed $\Loc(\Dbc)$ categories, proving (2). Here $j_!$ denotes its exact levelwise derived functor.

source.place: Proof (2): definition for the standard compactification and comparison with the chosen one.

proof.text: Identify the candidate right adjoint. The composition isomorphism of module pullbacks in [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] gives $j^*q^*\simeq(qj)^*=p^*$ on sheaves. These pullbacks are exact by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], so their derived versions in [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] are computed levelwise. Applying the sheaf composition isomorphism in every degree therefore gives the same natural isomorphism on arbitrary unbounded complexes, and then on their localizing subcategories. An exact levelwise pullback commutes with cohomological shifts: both complexes in degree $n$ have term $j^*(L^{n+2})$ and differential $j^*(d^{n+2})$. Apply the final assertion of [det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-twists] with $f=j$ and $K=q^*N$; $\ell$ is invertible since $p\ne\ell$. It gives $j^*((q^*N)(1))\simeq(j^*q^*N)(1)$. Combining these natural identifications yields $j^*(q^*N(1)[2])\simeq p^*N(1)[2]$ for every $N\in\Loc(\Dbc(V,\Lambda))$.

source.place: Proof (3): the identity $j^*q^*(1)[2]=p^*(1)[2]$, with coefficient category, twist and shift checked.

proof.text:
Use the adjunction $Rq_*\dashv q^*(1)[2]$ explicitly asserted by [det-prop-p1-adjunction-rational-triangle], applied over $Y=V$ with the same rational coefficient $\Lambda$. For $M\in\Loc(\Dbc(\mathbf A^1_V,\Lambda))$ and $N\in\Loc(\Dbc(V,\Lambda))$, steps 2–4 give
$$
\operatorname{Hom}(Rp_!M,N)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(Rq_*j_!M,N)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(j_!M,q^*N(1)[2])\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(M,j^*(q^*N(1)[2]))\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(M,p^*N(1)[2]).
$$
Every bijection is natural in $M,N$: the first and last are induced by the natural isomorphisms of steps 3 and 4, and the middle two are the Hom bijections of the projective-line and open adjunctions. Their inverses in reverse order give the inverse composite. This exhibits $Rp_!\dashv p^*(1)[2]$, including that the displayed right adjoint takes values in the required localizing category.

source.place: Proof (3): compose the two adjunctions through their natural Hom bijections.

proof.text: By [sk-prop-sf-existence], $p^!$ is a right adjoint of this same $Rp_!$ on $\Loc(\Dctf)$, hence on the equal $\Loc(\Dbc)$ categories of step 2. Apply [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] to $F=Rp_!$, $G=p^!$ and $J=p^*(1)[2]$, the latter adjunction being step 5. The $J$-transpose of the counit $Rp_!p^!N\to N$ gives the component $p^!N\to p^*N(1)[2]$; the cited statement makes these components natural, invertible and uniquely compatible with the counits. This proves the final assertion of (3).

source.place: Proof (3), final sentence: uniqueness of right adjoints and counit compatibility.

proof_origin.place: Proof (1)–(3), expanded into six steps; standard compactification comparison, category equality and natural Hom bijections made explicit.
